Definition: from G649; a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers):--apostle, messenger, he that is sent.
BiblicalUsage: An apostle is one sent with authority, and the word belongs first to the twelve Jesus named after a night of prayer. The church is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, God set apostles first in the church, and the New Jerusalem itself bears the twelve apostles' names on its foundations.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the apostles matter because they were eyewitnesses the risen Christ chose and sent, not volunteers who appointed themselves. Their foundation still holds the church up, and no new foundation is being laid.
